question: May I work from Spain for two weeks, and what must I arrange beforehand?
answer:
Based on the provided source passages, it appears that workation (working from abroad) is permitted within the EU, but there are certain requirements and limitations. According to NL-07:S1, workation is allowed for a maximum of ten working days per calendar year, and requests must be submitted at least 15 working days before the start date. However, approval is not guaranteed.

To work from abroad, both the manager and People Operations must give written approval, as stated in NL-07:S2. It is not possible to work from abroad without both approvals.

As for the specific request to work from Spain for two weeks, it is unclear whether this is feasible based on the provided information. The maximum allowed workation period is ten working days per calendar year, and it is not specified whether this can be extended or if there are any exceptions for longer periods.

To determine the feasibility of working from Spain for two weeks, it would be necessary to submit a request at least 15 working days before the start date and obtain approval from both the manager and People Operations.

sources.title: Working from Abroad
sources.heading: Workation
sources.text: Workation is permitted only within the EU for a maximum of ten working days per calendar year. Requests must be submitted at least 15 working days before the start date. Approval is not guaranteed.

sources.title: Working from Abroad
sources.heading: Approvals
sources.text: Both the manager and People Operations must give written approval before travel. Working from abroad is not permitted without both approvals. Document NL-06 alone does not constitute workation approval.

sources.title: Working Hours and Availability
sources.heading: Collaboration
sources.text: Shared availability hours are Monday to Friday, 10:00 to 15:00 German local time. Individual part-time agreements take precedence. Working time must be recorded daily in the time-tracking system.

sources.title: Remote Work Policy
sources.heading: Allowance
sources.text: Up to three remote-working days per calendar week are permitted with manager agreement. Required team meetings on site take priority. Unused remote-working days cannot be carried over to the following week.

sources.title: Support Hours and Escalation
sources.heading: Hours
sources.text: Regular support is available Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 German local time, excluding public holidays in Hamburg. Outside this window, P1 on-call support is available only to customers with an on-call support agreement.
